contract.reader: An engineer or student who knows finite differences (entries 1 to 3) and meets FEM in a code without knowing what it computes or why it converges
contract.problem: What the weak form is and why it allows meshes of any shape; what essential and natural boundary conditions mean; why Galerkin's method is accurate; what convergence rates to expect
contract.outcome: Derive a weak form with Dirichlet, Neumann or Robin conditions; assemble element matrices; state and check the rates h^d and h^(d+1); recognize when FEM and finite differences coincide and when FEM is worth its cost
contract.contribution: The method built in the order its theory needs, every element matrix written out, predicted orders measured for linear and quadratic elements, and the identity of linear triangles with the five-point matrix shown by computation
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; three scripts with real output; Brenner and Scott, Courant 1943, Hughes, Johnson, Strang and Fix, Zienkiewicz-Taylor-Zhu
contract.limitations: Linear elliptic model problems in one and two dimensions; adaptivity, non-smooth solutions, isoparametric and 3D elements described but not computed

findings.location: Section 1.2 weak form (desktop-light-03, mobile-light-05) and Section 1.1 model problem (desktop-light-02); at 360 px also Sections 2.1, 4.2, 5.1 (mobile-light-09, 18, 22)
findings.problem: At 1280 px the weak form stops after a(u,v) = integral k u'v' dx; the definition l(v) = integral f v dx + q_L v(L) is off the right edge with no cue, and the model problem loses '= q_L'. At 360 px the weak form stops at 'for all admissible', the Galerkin system loses 'KU = F', and the L2 estimate C' h^(d+1) is hidden
findings.whyItMatters: l(v) is where the flux (natural) condition enters, which the next bullet and Exercise 1 depend on; the L2 estimate is the result Sections 3.3 and 4.2 measure
findings.action: Put the weak-form statement, a(u,v) and l(v) on three lines; break the model problem before its boundary conditions; at 360 px split the Galerkin system, the two estimates and the 2D weak form
findings.acceptance: At 1280 px l(v) and k(L)u'(L) = q_L are visible without sideways scrolling; at 360 px the weak form, the L2 estimate and KU = F are visible without scrolling

findings.problem: At 1280 px the H1 orders of Section 3.3 are cut ('H1 1.') and the 'True' of the Section 5.3 stiffness-matrix comparison shows only on the first line
findings.whyItMatters: Small; the prose states both results
